calculator.ppmSafetyNote: Calculated under USDA FSIS and EU food safety standards.
calculator.saltpeterWarmWarning: CRITICAL: Saltpeter (KNO3) is strictly forbidden for thermal processing above 75°C (risk of carcinogenic nitrosamines NDMA). Use only for raw dry-cured meats!
calculator.trichinellaWarning: SAFETY MANDATE: Wild boar requires official veterinary artificial digestion testing for Trichinella spiralis.
calculator.trichinellaConfirm: I confirm official veterinary trichinella clearance
calculator.szynkowarInstructions: Cut meat into 3x3 cm cubes, massage with water and salts until tacky. Place in liner pouch, press spring, and cure 24h chilled.

smoking.title: Smoking & Scalding Assistant
smoking.dryingInstruction: Run the smoker with maximum air draft WITHOUT SMOKE at 45–55°C. Smoking wet meat causes bitter creosote condensation and black soot!
smoking.parchmentSurfaceConfirm: I confirm: meat surface is warm, dry, and feels like crisp parchment
smoking.waterTempAlert: WATER BATH TEMPERATURE ALERT! Water exceeds 82°C. Risk of fat rendering and moisture collapse!
smoking.processFinishedMsg: Thermal processing complete! Batch marked as Ready.
smoking.dryingTip: 💡 Butcher's Rule: Smoke applied to a damp surface causes tarry creosote deposition and a sour taste. Dry at 45–55°C with maximum draft.
smoking.waterOverheatMsg: Water temperature ({temp}°C) exceeds critical 82°C. Reduce heat to prevent fat rendering and jelly pockets!
smoking.coreTempReached: ✅ Target core temperature ({temp}°C) reached! Proceed immediately to shock cooling.
smoking.coolingInstruction: Submerge the hot product in ice-cold water (< 15°C) for 10–15 minutes. Shock cooling halts protein denaturation, tightens casing, and prevents wrinkling.
smoking.coolingTip: 🧊 After the cold bath, hang the smoked meat in a cool, ventilated place (12–15°C) until completely dry before placing in the refrigerator.
